guardFiles.policy: Reject missing, expired, inactive, and reset-required identities before tenant data.
Hash passwords, expire reset links, block reused reset tokens, and avoid secret logging.
Attach request id, actor id, company id, route id, and safe logger scope.
Resolve company scope server-side and block cross-company identifiers.
Check room grants for trackers, insights, import, governance, reports, and membership.
Keep values, agreement, LOA, negotiations, invoices, and forecast facts out of frontline routes.
Membership model, user seats, plan changes, and billing access remain admin-only.
Editors can update assigned tracker fields; viewers and inactive users cannot mutate.
Every denied sensitive action writes an immutable audit event.
Return consistent validation, auth, permission, tenant, conflict, and server envelopes.

handoff: Use this pack to create a private backend repo that starts with clear boundaries instead of a blank project.
The first commit should contain structure, docs, examples, workflows, and fixture contracts, not live secrets or customer data.
Route, migration, guard, and test batches are named so GitHub issues, pull requests, and CI jobs can share one vocabulary.
After the file pack is committed, the next implementation step is to standardize API error envelopes and audit event payloads.
